claims.text: The deviation is established on the field that governs. The GPS polyline between the recorded pickup event and the recorded drop-off event measures 27.69 km (trace_distance_km) against a booked optimal of 21.3 km, an excess of 6.39 km — 30.0% of optimal. That clears the 20% limb and clears the 0.8 km limb, so both establishment tests of POL-RD-01 pass and the deviation is ESTABLISHED. POL-RD-01 makes the trace figure the governing measurement and forbids citing the rounded 27.7 km on the trip record in its place; the two straddle nothing here, but the 27.69 km figure is the one the ruling must use.

The trace is unimpaired for policy purposes, so the measured excess stands and no independent corroboration is required. EV-GPS-02858 carries 218 fixes at a 10 second sample interval with 100.0% coverage and no gap at all between consecutive fixes (max_gap_sec 0.0, gaps list empty). None of limbs (a), (b) or (c) of POL-RD-07 fires: there is no gap above 90 seconds, no straight-line jump above 500 m and no sampling interval above 30 seconds. POL-RD-10(3) is therefore not engaged and the trace alone carries the excess.

The rider's initial burden is discharged under POL-RD-08. The trip record, the trace and the fare ledger are all filed under this trip's identifier and their timestamps cohere: the trace's first fix is 2026-08-23T08:41:14, exactly the trip record's started_at, and the fare ledger is charged at 09:17:49, 25 seconds after the record's ended_at of 09:17:24, for a total of 35.52 — the amount in dispute. The excess of 6.39 km meets the POL-RD-01 threshold on an unimpaired trace, so limb (b) is satisfied and the burden shifts to the driver. The rider's own 60-day counters (deviation_claims_60d 0, deviation_claims_60d_substantiated 0) are nowhere near the 4-or-more trigger, so POL-RD-08 imposes no additional corroboration requirement on this claim.

No exculpatory clause is open to the driver on this record. The chat log for the trip is empty — 0 messages, no first or last message timestamp — so POL-RD-04 cannot run: there is no rider instruction, no waypoint_hint to compare against the trace, and no rider-caused detour to exclude. The trip record likewise carries no amendment: pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at are both null and amended_optimal_distance_km is null, so POL-RD-05 cannot be invoked and no amended optimal displaces the booked 21.3 km. Nothing in the record excuses any part of the 6.39 km excess.

The driver's only explanation is 'Followed navigation'. That is an assertion, not a clause, and it is tested against the traffic advisory for this trip and nothing else. The bundle holds no advisory covering this trip at all: EV-ADVIS-02858-01 is MISSING, has no payload, and carries weight_multiplier 0.0 with issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT — its absence is itself citable. The comparison POL-RD-03 requires (an advisory naming a road or segment the optimal route traverses, with a validity window overlapping the time the trace shows the vehicle would have reached it, matched by a route that leaves and rejoins the corridor) therefore cannot be run, POL-RD-03 is unavailable, and the assertion carries no weight under POL-RD-08. Because the driver names no evidence ID for any advisory, POL-RD-13(1) applies: an assertion that cites no artifact cannot be an exculpatory clause invoked against a cited one, so the absent advisory is a gap in the bundle rather than a POL-RD-10(5) contradiction, and the case is ruled rather than escalated. The trace being unimpaired, POL-RD-13(2) governs: the deviation stands at the measured figure and POL-RD-02 runs against the booked optimal route.

The fare model and the product put this squarely in POL-RD-02. fare_model is METERED and quoted_fare_sgd is null, so POL-RD-11 does not displace the recomputation and no distance-or-time refund is closed off. vehicle_type is RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL, so POL-RD-12 does not apply either: the baseline for POL-RD-01 is the booked optimal of 21.3 km, and no distance attributable to collecting a co-rider is in issue.

On POL-RD-02 the refund is arithmetic. recomputed_fare = (3.80 + 0.75 x 21.3 + 0.28 x 28.8) x the surge_multiplier recorded on the FARE_BREAKDOWN + 0.80 platform fee + 0 ERP = 28.639; refund = charged_total 35.52 less 28.639 = 6.881. The surge multiplier was read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier (1.0) and from nowhere else — it is 1.0, so it neither doubles nor shrinks anything. The refund is above the 0.50 de minimis and is 19.4% of charged_total, far below the 90% full-refund share, so it is not a FULL_REFUND and intermediate values are not rounded: the payable sum, rounded UP to the nearest SGD 0.05, is 6.90.

Nothing is added on top of that figure. optimal_route_erp is 0.0, tolls_erp is 0.0, every ERP line is 0.00 and erp_gantries is empty, so there is no off-route gantry and no phantom gantry to correct as a standalone pass-through under POL-RD-09(4), and no airport surcharge on a trip that neither originates nor ends at an airport. POL-RD-09(1) forbids adding any pass-through line to the POL-RD-02 figure, so the 6.90 is the whole of the money the rider claims.

On quantum, candour about one point: the dispute form records 9.00 contested, while the policy arithmetic yields 6.90. The rider asks for the 6.90, not the balance of the 9.00, because POL-RD-02 fixes the refund as charged_total less the recomputed optimal-route fare and no clause on this record licenses a round figure or a discretionary sum beyond it. The outcome is PARTIAL_REFUND — part of the contested amount returned to the filing rider — and the refund leaves the rider no longer carrying the distance and time charges for the 6.39 km the driver drove beyond the optimal route.

claims.text: POL-RD-01 fixes the measured excess on the governing trace figure: EV-GPS-02858 records trace_distance_km 27.69 against the booked optimal 21.3 km on EV-TRIP-02858, an excess of 6.39 km, or 30.0% of optimal. That clears the establishment gate (more than 20% and more than 0.8 km) but falls well short of the materiality gate (more than 50% or more than 8.0 km). The consequence for the driver is bounded: this is a non-material deviation, so anything that moves is the POL-RD-02 arithmetic partial and nothing heavier is available on the finding.

The arithmetic caps the money well below the SGD 9.00 the rider contests. Under POL-RD-02, with the fare model METERED on EV-FARE-02858 and the surge multiplier read from that same artifact at 1.000, recomputed_fare = (3.80 + 0.75 x 21.3 + 0.28 x 28.8) x 1.000 + 0.80 = 28.639 against a charged_total of 35.52, leaving 6.881, which rounds up to 6.90. That is 19.37% of the charged amount — nowhere near the 90% that would convert the ruling into a FULL_REFUND. The rider's claimed figure is overstated on the face of the ledger.

Nothing may be added on top of that arithmetic figure. EV-FARE-02858 carries zero ERP gantry lines and an off-optimal-route ERP total of 0.00, no airport surcharge, and no charge line lacking a counterpart in EV-GPS-02858 or EV-TRIP-02858, so POL-RD-09(4) has no phantom line to correct and POL-RD-10(8) is not engaged. POL-RD-09(1) in any event forbids adding an off-route ERP line on top of the POL-RD-02 refund, because that refund is already charged_total less a recomputed fare built only on on-optimal-route charges.

No repeat-deviation uplift and no conduct referral is available on this record. The deviation is not MATERIAL under POL-RD-01, so POL-RD-06's profile check is not even triggered; and on the POL-RD-06 test itself the driver's trailing-90-day figure is 1 deviation flag against 309 completed trips on EV-DPROF-02858 — a ratio of 0.003, far below the 0.05 ratio and below the 3-flag count the clause requires. POL-GEN-01 confines this test to driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d and driver_profile.completed_trips_90d; the lifetime prior_deviation_flags counter is a near-synonym trap and may not be substituted. The rider therefore cannot reach FULL_REFUND through the pattern route.

The rider's own initial burden is not made out on the artifacts. POL-RD-08(a) requires the artifacts to describe the same trip with a matching trip identifier across trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown, and EV-FARE-02858 carries two identifiers: its envelope reads TRP-02858 while its own payload reads TRP-02758. That payload identifier does not match the TRP-02858 on EV-TRIP-02858 and EV-GPS-02858. The mismatch is a matter of record, not of argument, and on a rider-filed dispute a failure of the claimant's burden leaves the CHARGED status and the zero refund_issued_sgd on EV-FARE-02858 exactly as they stand under POL-GEN-03.

In the alternative, that same mismatch is a mandatory escalation and no monetary outcome should issue. POL-RD-10(2) directs the Judge NOT to rule where the trip identifiers on trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown do not all match, and under POL-GEN-03 an ESCALATE is terminal: it replaces the ruling, no refund issues, and the disputed amount is held rather than collected or refunded. That result protects the driver's settled position on this trip while a human reviewer resolves which identifier governs.

ruling.explanation:
To the rider and the driver: both of you agree on the arithmetic, and so do I, so this is a short case on the money and a longer one on the defences.

THE FINDING. The measurement that governs is the GPS trace, EV-GPS-02858: 27.69 km between the recorded pickup and drop-off, against the booked optimal route of 21.3 km on EV-TRIP-02858 (POL-RD-01 says the trace figure governs over the rounded 27.7 km copy on the trip record). That is 6.39 km and 30.0% over. Both POL-RD-01 establishment tests pass (more than 20% and more than 0.8 km), so the deviation is ESTABLISHED. It is not a MATERIAL deviation (not more than 50%, not more than 8.0 km), and the trace is not impaired for policy purposes: 218 fixes at a 10-second interval, 100% coverage, no gaps, so POL-RD-07 and POL-RD-10(3) are not engaged.

THE MONEY. The fare model on EV-FARE-02858 is METERED, so POL-RD-02 applies. Taking the surge multiplier from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier on that same artifact (1.0, read from nowhere else): recomputed_fare = (3.80 + 0.75 x 21.3 + 0.28 x 28.8) x 1.0 + 0.80 platform fee = 28.639. charged_total was 35.52. Refund = 35.52 - 28.639 = 6.881, above the 0.50 de minimis and 19.4% of the charge — far below the 90% that would make it a full refund — so the payable amount, rounded up to the nearest 0.05, is 6.90. Nothing is added on top: there are no ERP gantry lines, no tolls and no airport surcharge, so POL-RD-09(1) forbids any add-on and POL-RD-09(4) has no phantom line to correct. The rider asked for 6.90 rather than the 9.00 on the dispute form, and 6.90 is the whole of the remedy; the claim for the balance is not supported by any clause.

THE DRIVER'S DEFENCES. The chat log EV-CHAT-02858 is empty (0 messages), so POL-RD-04 has no rider instruction to work with and no waypoint_hint to test; the trip record shows pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at both null and amended_optimal_distance_km null, so POL-RD-05 cannot be run. The only explanation offered is 'Followed navigation'. No traffic advisory covers this trip: EV-ADVIS-02858-01 is MISSING, weight_multiplier 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT. POL-RD-03 therefore cannot be run and the assertion carries no weight under POL-RD-08 (an assertion that cites no artifact discharges nothing). Because no advisory was cited by the driver, POL-RD-13(1) applies: an uncited traffic assertion is a gap in the bundle, not a POL-RD-10(5) contradiction, so the case is ruled and not escalated, and POL-RD-13(2) leaves the deviation standing at the measured figure.

THE IDENTIFIER POINT (the driver's two alternative arguments). I have checked it. EV-FARE-02858 is filed under this trip's identifier TRP-02858; its line is charged at 09:17:49, 25 seconds after this trip's ended_at of 09:17:24, for exactly the 35.52 in dispute, and its charged distance and time (27.7 km, 36.2 min) match the trip record. The string 'TRP-02758' inside its payload is contradicted by the rest of that same artifact. The three artifacts do carry matching trip identifiers, so the rider's initial burden under POL-RD-08(a) is discharged and POL-RD-10(2) does not fire. I record the inconsistency here rather than in the referrals list: no clause produces a referral for it, and the platform should correct the ledger payload so the artifact reconciling to this trip reads TRP-02858 throughout. For completeness, no other POL-RD-10 trigger fires: the trace is unimpaired (10(3)), the money is nowhere near the 10(6) ceiling, the timestamps cohere (10(4)), and every charge line has a counterpart in the trace and trip record (10(8)).

REPEAT-DEVIATION UPLIFT AND CONDUCT REFERRAL. None is available. The deviation is not material, so the POL-RD-06 check is not even triggered, and on its own test the driver's trailing-90-day figures on EV-DPROF-02858 (1 deviation flag, 309 completed trips) fall far below both the 3-flag and the 0.05-ratio thresholds. The lifetime prior_deviation_flags counter is context only under POL-GEN-01 and has not been used.

OUTCOME AND NEXT STEPS. The rider is refunded 6.90; the driver is owed nothing — the ledger billed 27.7 km against a trace of 27.69 km, so there is no unbilled-distance shortfall under POL-RD-04. The confidence cap is set by the artifacts carrying the deciding facts (EV-GPS-02858, EV-TRIP-02858 and EV-FARE-02858, all at weight 1.0); the missing advisory carries no fact and does not cap it. The monetary effect (6.90) is below the 8.00 execution threshold, so it is released on issue. Either party may appeal once within 30 days under POL-GEN-04.

ledger.claim: The rider's own initial burden is not made out on the artifacts. POL-RD-08(a) requires the artifacts to describe the same trip with a matching trip identifier across trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown, and EV-FARE-02858 carries two identifiers: its envelope reads TRP-02858 while its own payload reads TRP-02758. That payload identifier does not match the TRP-02858 on EV-TRIP-02858 and EV-GPS-02858. The mismatch is a matter of record, not of argument, and on a rider-filed dispute a failure of the claimant's burden leaves the CHARGED status and the zero refund_issued_sgd on EV-FARE-02858 exactly as they stand under POL-GEN-03.

In the alternative, that same mismatch is a mandatory escalation and no monetary outcome should issue. POL-RD-10(2) directs the Judge NOT to rule where the trip identifiers on trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown do not all match, and under POL-GEN-03 an ESCALATE is terminal: it replaces the ruling, no refund issues, and the disputed amount is held rather than collected or refunded. That result protects the driver's settled position on this trip while a human reviewer resolves which identifier governs.
